compiler.method: Scan every object property named type; collect string literals and conditional branches; classify fields enums (including helper arguments) and connection metadata separately; find functions/methods/local arrows with parameters named type/resourceType and collect static literals at matching call sites; include literal XML block/shadow type attributes. types excludes known procedure metadata ROUND/NORMAL/Label/String, fields enums and connection metadata.
limitations: This is a conservative static inventory, not an exhaustive proof of all runtime-generated block types.
Dynamic expressions (spec.type, variables, imports, concatenation, templates with substitutions) are recorded but not evaluated or followed by full interprocedural dataflow.
Helper calls are matched by AST function name, not a bound TypeScript symbol; shadowed names could introduce false positives.
Spec/metadata versus block classification is heuristic; allStaticTypeStrings intentionally includes non-block metadata/field enum values for auditability.
Only ts/compile-ts.mjs is scanned; Rust assembly, imported modules, editor/runtime conversions and future computed paths can add types.
Finite literals in conditional branches are included even when a branch is unreachable for current samples; sample runtime coverage must be compared separately.
